question: The directive asks whether ViciOne.ServiceBus.Analyzers.Package really needs its netstandard2.0 target, and requires proof that its analyzer package bytes and layout stay correct. It was packed both ways and the two packages were compared.
command: dotnet pack src/ViciOne.ServiceBus.Analyzers.Package/ViciOne.ServiceBus.Analyzers.Package.csproj -c Release -o <directory>, then unzip and sha256 every entry
note: The net10.0 pack needed a lock file evaluated for that framework: dotnet restore -p:RestoreLockedMode=false --force-evaluate. Both the project file and the lock file were written back from a byte snapshot afterwards and compared.

layout.note: The package also carries a nuspec, [Content_Types].xml, _rels/.rels and one psmdcp part whose file name NuGet generates per pack; that name is the only layout difference and it differs between two packs of the same source as well.

nuspecDifference.reading: An analyzer package carries no lib/ folder, so this empty dependency group is what NuGet reads to decide which projects may reference the package. net10.0 narrows that set, which is a capability change, and the directive forbids one.

conclusion: The target stays netstandard2.0. What changes is the name of the exception: the project is not a compiler host, it is the package whose framework group is a consumer surface, and it declares ViciOneAnalyzerPackageSurface. The analyzer and its code fixes declare the standard IsRoslynComponent.

afterTheChange.reading: The package produced after this block hashes identically to the one produced before it, so the vocabulary change altered no package byte.
